title: Scaling out a service that was blocked on the database
wrong_assumption: Latency is high, so the service needs more replicas.
actual_cause: Every replica held its own fixed database connection pool, so adding replicas pushed total connections past the database limit and new connections queued.
what_we_did: Doubled the replica count twice during a live incident.
what_we_should_have_done: Checked connection pool saturation and database wait events before changing replica count.
lesson: Healthy CPU with bad latency means waiting, not computing. Find what is being waited on before adding capacity.
mistake_to_avoid: Treating horizontal scaling as a default remedy for every latency problem.

title: Adding retries at every layer of the call chain
wrong_assumption: Each service becomes more resilient if it retries failed calls on its own.
actual_cause: Retries multiply along the call chain, so one user action generated tens of downstream requests and kept a recovering database saturated.
what_we_did: Enabled generous independent retry policies in each service, with no shared budget.
what_we_should_have_done: Kept retries at the edge only, with jittered exponential backoff and a global retry budget.
lesson: Local resilience decisions can combine into global fragility. Model the whole call graph before setting retry policy.
mistake_to_avoid: Configuring retries service by service without multiplying them across the full chain.

title: Trusting a single-point soil resistivity survey
wrong_assumption: One resistivity measurement is representative of the whole site.
actual_cause: The measurement was taken in an unrepresentative low-resistivity pocket, so the earthing grid was designed on an input roughly three times lower than reality.
what_we_did: Designed and installed the full earthing grid from that single survey.
what_we_should_have_done: Measured resistivity at multiple locations and depths, and across seasons, before fixing the design basis.
lesson: A compliant calculation built on wrong input data is still an unsafe installation. Verify inputs, not just arithmetic.
mistake_to_avoid: Accepting convenience-sampled site data as a design basis.

title: Monitoring a gearbox with the wrong vibration metric
wrong_assumption: Overall RMS vibration level is a sufficient health indicator for a multi-stage gearbox.
actual_cause: Early gear tooth damage appears as small sidebands around gear mesh frequency, which barely change the overall RMS value until failure is imminent.
what_we_did: Ran a weekly vibration route with alarms configured only on overall RMS velocity.
what_we_should_have_done: Added spectrum and envelope analysis at gear mesh frequency and its sidebands.
lesson: Match the measurement to the failure mode. Monitoring that cannot see the failure mode is paperwork, not protection.
mistake_to_avoid: Reading a green dashboard as proof of health without checking what it actually measures.

title: Hiding a hardware noise fault behind a firmware watchdog
wrong_assumption: Random resets in the field are a firmware stability problem.
actual_cause: Conducted noise from the customer's switching charger coupled into an unfiltered reset line on the board.
what_we_did: Added watchdog timers and reset counters, which masked the symptom for two months.
what_we_should_have_done: Reproduced the real field environment on the bench, including the actual charger and cable, before changing any code.
lesson: If a defect will not reproduce, fix the test environment first. Software workarounds on hardware problems destroy the evidence.
mistake_to_avoid: Debugging in the layer that is easiest to change rather than the layer that contains the fault.

title: Replacing a failing component instead of re-deriving its operating conditions
wrong_assumption: Repeated impeller erosion means the impeller material is not hard enough.
actual_cause: A plant throughput increase pushed available NPSH below required NPSH, so the pump cavitated in normal operation.
what_we_did: Spent two years replacing impellers and upgrading materials.
what_we_should_have_done: Recalculated suction hydraulics at the new flow rate as soon as the second identical failure appeared.
lesson: Identical repeat failures point at the system, not the part. Every capacity change invalidates the assumptions around it.
mistake_to_avoid: Letting a maintenance budget absorb a design problem indefinitely.

title: Dropping an index judged unused by reading the code
wrong_assumption: An index is unused because no query in the codebase names it.
actual_cause: A composite index was serving a query the search missed, so the planner fell back to a sequential scan on 40 million rows.
what_we_did: Dropped the index as part of a routine migration.
what_we_should_have_done: Checked database index usage statistics before dropping anything.
lesson: The application does not know what the query planner chose. Prove it from database statistics.
mistake_to_avoid: Deciding what the database needs by grepping application code.

title: Setting one TTL for every cache key at deploy time
wrong_assumption: A fixed 24 hour cache TTL spreads load evenly.
actual_cause: Every key was written in the same deploy window, so all keys expired at the same instant and the database took the whole load at once.
what_we_did: Scaled the service twice to absorb a weekly CPU spike.
what_we_should_have_done: Added jitter to the TTL and a stale-while-revalidate window.
lesson: Anything expiring on a fixed schedule eventually expires all at once. Spread expiry deliberately.
mistake_to_avoid: Reading a perfectly periodic spike as a capacity problem.

title: Granting production access permanently during incidents
wrong_assumption: Access granted in an emergency will be cleaned up afterwards.
actual_cause: There was no expiry mechanism, so every emergency grant became permanent and standing write access grew to 60 accounts.
what_we_did: Granted individual permissions during incidents for three years.
what_we_should_have_done: Made emergency access time-bound and self-expiring from the start.
lesson: Access granted under pressure must expire on its own. Nothing that depends on remembering will survive.
mistake_to_avoid: Treating revocation as a follow-up task rather than an automatic behaviour.

title: Treating every critical CVE as an emergency
wrong_assumption: A critical severity score means every affected service is at critical risk.
actual_cause: Only two of eleven services could reach the vulnerable code path with untrusted input.
what_we_did: Scheduled out-of-hours emergency patching across all eleven services.
what_we_should_have_done: Checked call reachability per service before deciding urgency.
lesson: A CVE score describes the worst case for anyone. Reachability decides urgency for you.
mistake_to_avoid: Letting a scanner set your incident priority without analysis.

title: Writing a health check that cannot fail
wrong_assumption: A passing readiness probe means the service is working.
actual_cause: The probe only confirmed the process was alive and never touched the database connection, so a pod with an empty connection pool still reported ready.
what_we_did: Investigated every service except the one that was actually broken, for forty minutes.
what_we_should_have_done: Made the probe assert its critical dependency with a short timeout.
lesson: A health check should assert something that can actually break.
mistake_to_avoid: Trusting a probe you have never seen fail.

title: Trusting a green pipeline as proof of deployment
wrong_assumption: If the deploy stage passes, the new build is running.
actual_cause: The deploy pushed to a registry tag the cluster no longer pulled from, so a fix sat undeployed for six days while reported as shipped.
what_we_did: Told stakeholders the fix was live based on pipeline status.
what_we_should_have_done: Added a post-deploy check querying the running service for its build identifier.
lesson: Verify the outcome, not the process. Green steps are a claim, not evidence.
mistake_to_avoid: Confusing 'the pipeline ran' with 'the system changed'.

title: Approving a plant modification without a relief review
wrong_assumption: A small mechanical addition does not affect the safety case.
actual_cause: Adding a downstream pump made blocked outlet the governing relief scenario, needing roughly twice the installed relief area.
what_we_did: Approved the 2015 modification through the normal mechanical route.
what_we_should_have_done: Required a relief system review as part of modification approval.
lesson: A small change can move the governing safety scenario. Tie safety review to the change process.
mistake_to_avoid: Assuming a safety study stays valid after the plant it describes has changed.

title: Monitoring whether a data job finished instead of whether it was right
wrong_assumption: A pipeline that exits cleanly has produced correct output.
actual_cause: An inner join silently dropped work orders whose asset had been renamed, understating reports by 30% for two months.
what_we_did: Alerted only on job exit codes.
what_we_should_have_done: Added row count and join-match assertions between stages.
lesson: Green pipelines are not correct pipelines. Correctness needs its own assertions.
mistake_to_avoid: Monitoring liveness and calling it data quality.

title: Rolling back before capturing any evidence
wrong_assumption: Rolling back is always the safe first move in an incident.
actual_cause: The rollback restored service but destroyed the query plans that would have identified the cause, so the same failure returned two weeks later.
what_we_did: Rolled back immediately on every latency incident.
what_we_should_have_done: Captured plans, metrics and a heap snapshot before rolling back.
lesson: Rollback is a mitigation, not a diagnosis. Capture evidence first when the system is still failing.
mistake_to_avoid: Losing the only reproduction you will get.

title: Estimating a migration from the staging dataset
wrong_assumption: If it takes four minutes in staging it will take about the same in production.
actual_cause: Staging held 2% of production rows and no index bloat, so the migration that took four minutes there locked a production table for fifty minutes.
what_we_did: Scheduled a 15 minute maintenance window based on staging timings.
what_we_should_have_done: Rehearsed against a production-sized restored snapshot.
lesson: Time an operation against realistic data volume, or you are timing the wrong thing.
mistake_to_avoid: Treating staging as a scale model when it is only a shape model.

title: Letting each team choose its own alert thresholds
wrong_assumption: Teams know their own services, so local thresholds are best.
actual_cause: Thresholds drifted until 70% of pages were non-actionable, and responders started acknowledging alerts without reading them.
what_we_did: Allowed threshold changes with no review for two years.
what_we_should_have_done: Set a shared standard for what deserves a page, and reviewed alerts monthly.
lesson: Alert fatigue is a design failure, not a discipline failure.
mistake_to_avoid: Measuring alerting by coverage instead of by actionability.

title: Assuming a load test proved production capacity
wrong_assumption: Passing a load test at twice peak means the system handles twice peak.
actual_cause: The test used ten warm connections and cached responses, so it never exercised connection setup or cold caches.
what_we_did: Signed off capacity for a sale event on that result.
what_we_should_have_done: Load tested with realistic connection churn and a cold cache.
lesson: A load test is only as honest as the conditions it recreates.
mistake_to_avoid: Testing the happy path at volume and calling it capacity.
